subject: general
question: Select the correct pair of example of 'sublimation'.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Camphor and napthalene**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sublimation** is a chemical process where a substance transitions directly from the **solid phase** to the **gas phase** without passing through the intermediate **liquid phase**.
 
• **Camphor** is a transparent or white waxy solid with a strong aromatic odor. It is a **terpenoid** that readily undergoes **sublimation** at **room temperature** and standard **atmospheric pressure**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct regarding camphor.***
 
• **Naphthalene** is an **organic compound** with the formula **C10H8**. It is most commonly known as the primary ingredient in **mothballs**. Because it is composed of **non-polar molecules** held together by weak **van der Waals forces**, it sublimes easily into a toxic gas to repel moths. ***Hence, statement 1 is also correct regarding naphthalene.***
 
• **Salt** (specifically **Sodium Chloride**) and **Sugar** (**Sucrose**) do not exhibit sublimation under normal conditions. **Salt** has a very high **melting point** of about **801 degrees Celsius**, and **Sugar** typically melts or **decomposes** (caramelizes) when heated rather than subliming. ***Hence, statements 2, 3, and 4 are incorrect because they include non-sublimable substances like salt or sugar.***
 
• The pair **Camphor and naphthalene** is the most accurate example because both substances share the specific physical property of having a high **vapor pressure** at low temperatures, allowing them to turn into vapors directly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dry Ice:** This is the **solid form** of **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**. It is one of the most common examples of sublimation used in **refrigeration** and theatrical **fog effects**. It sublimes at a temperature of **-78.5 degrees Celsius** (**-109.3 degrees Fahrenheit**).
 
• **Ammonium Chloride:** This is a **white crystalline salt** that is highly soluble in water. In a laboratory setting, **Ammonium Chloride (NH4Cl)** is frequently used to demonstrate sublimation, as it appears to sublime upon heating (though it actually undergoes **thermal decomposition** into **Ammonia** and **Hydrogen Chloride** gas which then recombines).
 
• **Iodine:** At **standard temperature**, **Iodine** exists as dark-gray/purple-black lustrous **solids**. When heated gently, it produces a distinct **violet-colored vapor** through the process of **sublimation**.
 
• **Anthracene:** A solid **polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon** consisting of three fused benzene rings. It is used in the production of the red dye **alizarin** and is another classic example of a substance that undergoes **sublimation**.
 
• **Deposition:** This is the **reverse process** of sublimation. It occurs when a gas transforms directly into a solid without becoming a liquid. A common natural example of this is the formation of **frost** on a window or **snow** in clouds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vapor Pressure:** Sublimation occurs when the **vapor pressure** of a solid substance is high enough that molecules can escape into the gas phase even at temperatures below the **melting point**.
 
• **Triple Point:** In a **phase diagram**, sublimation happens at temperatures and pressures below the **triple point** of a substance, which is the specific condition where all three phases (solid, liquid, and gas) coexist in **equilibrium**.
 
• **Applications:** The principle of sublimation is utilized in **freeze-drying** (lyophilization) of food and pharmaceuticals. By freezing the material and then reducing the surrounding pressure, the **frozen water** (ice) sublimes directly into vapor, preserving the structure and nutritional value of the **product**.
 
• **Purification:** **Sublimation** is also a technique used by **chemists** to **purify compounds**. A solid is heated to vaporize it, and the vapor is then condensed onto a **cold surface**, leaving non-volatile impurities behind.
